PROVED, Section 6: log_2 W(d) = gamma d + O(log d) with gamma = lambda H(1/lambda) about 1.5056, lambda = log_2 3 and H the binary entropy function, so the normalized relative density decays at the explicit rate c = lambda(1 - H(1/lambda)) about 0.0793 bits per unit weight, in the information-theoretic form c = lambda D(1/lambda, 1/2); by a cycle-lemma argument plus standard entropy estimates, with a length-basis analogue also given. That rate is the length-basis eta of lagarias-1985-3x+1-problem divided by beta: eta/beta = 0.0793185. CONJECTURED, Section 7, Conjecture 7.1: W(d) = Theta(d^(-3/2) 2^(gamma d)), because over 100 <= d <= 10000 the residual log_2 W(d) - gamma d agrees with the ballot-type correction -(3/2) log_2 d to within 0.3 bits. THIS IS THE PRIOR STATEMENT OF THE d^(-3/2). It is a Theta, in the weight basis, numerically motivated and not proved, and its 0.3-bit tolerance is wide enough to absorb a bounded oscillating prefactor without seeing one. No oscillation, no almost-periodicity, no amplitude constant.
